title: Modules, Providers, and Version Pinning
intro: Real Terraform code is built from reusable modules and depends on provider plugins — both of which change over time. Controlling those versions is what keeps a plan from mysteriously changing between Tuesday and Wednesday.

steps.prompt: Check the Terraform CLI version and installed provider versions.
steps.fake_output:
Terraform v1.9.5
on linux_amd64
+ provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws v5.31.0
+ provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/random v3.6.0
steps.explanation: Both the core binary and each provider have independent versions.
steps.why: Pasting this output into bug reports and incident notes saves a round-trip — 'which version were you on?' is always the first question.

steps.prompt: Show which providers this configuration requires, and which modules require them.
steps.explanation: ~> 5.0 means 'any 5.x, but not 6.0' — the root module pins the major version.
steps.why: This tree explains conflicts: if one module demands aws >= 6.0 and another ~> 5.0, init fails, and this is how you see who's asking for what.

steps.prompt: You added a new module block from the registry. Download it (and update existing modules to their newest allowed versions).
steps.explanation: Modules are downloaded into .terraform/modules — same as providers go into .terraform/providers.
steps.why: 'terraform init' also downloads new modules. Always pin module versions (version = "6.4.0") in real code — an unpinned registry module can change underneath you on any future init.

steps.prompt: Upgrade providers to the newest versions allowed by your version constraints.
steps.fake_output:
Initializing provider plugins...
- Finding hashicorp/aws versions matching "~> 5.0"...
- Installing hashicorp/aws v5.68.0...

Terraform has made some changes to the provider dependency selections recorded in the .terraform.lock.hcl file.
steps.explanation: Moves from 5.31.0 to 5.68.0 — still within ~> 5.0 — and updates the lock file.
steps.why: Without -upgrade, init keeps using exactly the versions recorded in .terraform.lock.hcl, which is the point of the lock file. Upgrading is a deliberate act: do it, run plan, and commit the updated lock file in its own change.

steps.prompt: Record provider checksums for every platform your team uses (Linux CI runners and Mac laptops) in the lock file.
steps.fake_output:
- Obtained hashicorp/aws checksums for linux_amd64
- Obtained hashicorp/aws checksums for darwin_arm64
Success! Terraform has updated the lock file.
steps.explanation: The lock file now contains verified checksums for both platforms.
steps.why: Otherwise a lock file generated on a Mac only has Mac checksums, and CI on Linux fails with checksum mismatches — a very common 'works on my machine' Terraform problem.
